data.title: Research Lead, Predictive Oncology
data.description:
About Orakl Oncology

At Orakl Oncology, we combine patient-derived tumor models, experimental drug screening and computational modelling to improve oncology drug development. Our research brings together functional treatment-response measurements, molecular profiles and clinical information where available, creating opportunities to investigate how experimental responses translate into patient outcomes. Our platforms are designed to help anticipate clinical trial outcomes, evaluate therapies and identify new therapeutic opportunities.

Our mission is simple yet ambitious: to bring more effective treatments to patients who need them and to make drug development smarter, faster, and more personalised. We collaborate with top hospitals, research institutes, and pharmaceutical companies worldwide. Backed by leading investors, we are a fast-growing, mission-driven startup at the intersection of science and technology.

About the Role

We are looking for a Research Lead - Predictive Oncology, to build and lead a research programme to improve the translational capabilities of Orakl Oncology’s platform, and to provide the scientific backbone of O-Predict, Orakl’s predictive solutions.

You will own O-Predict's long-term scientific roadmap, choose the questions we pursue, and lead the work needed to answer them. The opportunity combines access to Orakl's experimental and molecular data, clinical information where available, and the ability to shape future data generation with our experimental and clinical collaborators.

This is a hands-on scientific leadership role. You will develop and test methods, mentor contributors, and build a coherent body of research with a recognisable scientific contribution. Publications, presentations and external collaborations will be integral outputs of that programme.

You will work closely with the CTO and our Data Science, Computational Biology, experimental, product and engineering colleagues. Your research will establish which predictions are reliable, identify their limitations, and inform how O-Predict can support drug-development decisions.

The role is suited to a researcher ready to take ownership of an independent programme within a collaborative company, including an emerging research leader with a strong record of original work.

What You'll Do

Own O-Predict's long-term research roadmap: define and maintain a 2-year scientific agenda, translated into a prioritised 12-month execution plan. Identify the key uncertainties, research hypotheses, data requirements, dependencies and resources; set milestones and explicit criteria for continuing, redirecting or stopping projects. Review priorities with the CTO as evidence and company needs evolve.

Lead R&D execution: take research programmes from question formulation through method development, validation and interpretation. Coordinate agreed contributions across Data Science, Computational Biology and experimental teams, establish project ownership, run scientific reviews, resolve blockers and mentor researchers. Remain hands-on in the analyses and modelling decisions that determine scientific quality.

Shape future data generation: identify the experiments, measurements and cohorts that would resolve important scientific uncertainties. Co-design these studies with experimental and clinical colleagues, prioritise them within the agreed research allocation, and use the results to test and revise your hypotheses.

Advance O-Predict's predictive capabilities: investigate how drug screening, patient-derived models, molecular and clinical data can improve treatment-response and trial-outcome predictions. Assess extensions to new cohorts, indications and therapeutic settings, specifying the evidence needed before extending claims.

Own the validation strategy: define relevant endpoints, external baselines and evaluation protocols. Lead independent and prospective validation plans with clinical and experimental collaborators, and document both performance and failure modes.

Connect research to product development: work with product and engineering colleagues to translate promising findings into reproducible methods and clearly documented scientific requirements. Define the evidence needed for transfer into O-Predict and assess feasibility, expected value and limitations.

Lead publications and scientific materials: build a publication and conference plan around the research roadmap. Lead manuscripts from analysis and figures through submission and reviewer responses, with contributions distributed across the research team. Produce abstracts, posters, talks and methods notes; provide scientific direction and review for partner evidence decks.

Build substantive scientific collaborations: work directly with clinical investigators and quantitative researchers to formulate questions, co-design studies, access complementary expertise and pursue independent validation opportunities. Represent O-Predict at relevant oncology and computational conferences, present your team's research, and turn scientific discussions into joint projects and publications.

Run publication governance: coordinate authorship and co-author review with hospital and pharmaceutical partners, track contractual publication and acknowledgement obligations, and align disclosure with confidentiality, patient-data permissions and intellectual-property considerations.

Minimum Qualifications

  • PhD, PharmD, MD, or MSc with an equivalent research record in a quantitative or biomedical discipline relevant to predictive oncology.

  • Demonstrated ownership of a research programme: you have formulated a scientific agenda, prioritised competing questions and led projects from initial hypothesis to validated findings.

  • Experience leading and mentoring scientific contributors, including coordinating work across disciplines and critically reviewing others' methods and conclusions.

  • A strong publication record in translational oncology, computational biology, biostatistics and/or ML for health, with clear intellectual and analytical contributions.

  • Hands-on proficiency in Python and SQL: you can work with internal data and libraries, develop and evaluate methods, and produce reproducible analyses and figures.

  • Strong grounding in statistical inference, predictive modelling and study design; able to challenge biological assumptions and machine-learning evaluations.

  • Excellent scientific writing and oral communication in English, including manuscripts, scientific presentations and substantive discussions with external researchers.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience leading R&D in a biotech, health technology or translational research setting, with responsibility for milestones and resource planning.

  • Experience translating research methods into a predictive product or decision-support workflow.

  • Familiarity with patient-derived models, drug sensitivity assays, clinical trial design and oncology endpoints.

  • Experience with independent or prospective validation, multimodal data integration, survival modelling, or pharmacological modelling.

  • Experience establishing academic or clinical collaborations and publishing with pharmaceutical partners.

  • Familiarity with appropriate reporting standards and reproducibility practices, including protocol registration and code and data availability statements.

  • Experience presenting research at oncology or computational conferences and maintaining an active scientific network.

Who You Are

  • A scientific owner: you turn an ambitious objective into a focused research agenda and make explicit choices about what deserves the team's time.

  • A hands-on leader: you develop others while staying close enough to the data and code to challenge results and solve difficult problems.

  • Rigorous and intellectually honest: you seek evidence that could disprove your hypotheses, distinguish exploratory findings from validated claims, and report limitations clearly.

  • Curious across disciplines: you connect experimental biology, clinical questions and quantitative methods.

  • An effective collaborator: you build productive relationships, navigate scientific disagreement and turn external discussions into research progress.

Why Join Orakl

  • Own a research programme with a clear scientific identity. Shape O-Predict's direction and build a body of work around the translation of experimental treatment responses into clinical predictions.

  • Study a distinctive combination of data. Bring together patient-derived tumor models, functional drug screening and molecular profiles, incorporating clinical information where available. Explore questions that require these modalities to be studied together.

  • Help decide what gets measured next. Work with experimental and clinical colleagues to design new studies that test your ideas and address the limitations of existing data.

  • Work across disciplines every day. Develop methods alongside the scientists generating the measurements, the engineers supporting their use, and collaborators who understand the clinical questions.

  • Build your scientific reputation. Lead original research, manuscripts and conference contributions, and develop sustained collaborations around your programme.

  • Connect discoveries to consequential decisions. Develop and validate methods intended to inform therapy evaluation and clinical development, with a clear account of what the evidence does and does not support.

  • Grow as a research leader. Mentor researchers and help shape the capabilities and future team needed to deliver the programme.

Interview Process

  1. HR Call: Align on motivation, role scope and expectations.

  2. Scientific Deep Dive: Discuss a research programme you led: the questions you chose, your own technical contributions, validation decisions, team leadership and published outcomes. We will share a confidential scientific briefing on O-Predict's current evidence, available data and open questions so you can assess the opportunity.

  3. Research Strategy and Analysis Discussion: Using a bounded, representative evidence package, discuss research priorities and a validation plan, critique an analysis, and outline how you would communicate the findings. Meet the experimental and computational colleagues you would work with and discuss the studies you would want to pursue.

  4. Reference Call: Speak with one or two close collaborators who can assess scientific judgement, research ownership and leadership.

  5. Founder Interview: Discuss O-Predict's scientific direction, decision-making responsibilities, research resources, publication arrangements and mutual ambitions.

data.description:
Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable. Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain.

Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.

 L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.

 

À Mines Saint-Étienne, nos centres de recherche sont le cœur battant de notre École.

Pensés comme de véritables hubs d’innovation, nos cinq Centres de Formation et de Recherche  articulent leurs expertises autour de grands enjeux industriels, environnementaux, sociétaux et technologiques.

Leur mission ? Imaginer le monde de demain en alliant excellence académique et impact concret.

Vous rêvez d’une industrie propre, efficace et durable ? Le centre SPIN en fait sa priorité.

Énergie, environnement, procédés industriels… on y conçoit des systèmes pour produire mieux, avec moins.

L’objectif ? Limiter l’impact environnemental, réduire la consommation énergétique et booster l’efficacité.

🔧 Dans un monde en pleine mutation, nos équipes déploient leur créativité scientifique pour accompagner l’industrie du futur. 

Et vous, prêt·e à innover à nos côtés ?

En tant qu’ Ingénieur(e), vous êtes au cœur de nos missions en recherche et innovation affecté au Centre SPIN. Au sein de ce centre, vous conjuguez passion scientifique et impact sociétal afin de contribuer à l’atteinte des objectifs de neutralité carbone de la France.

Le centre SPIN est l’un des centres de recherche de Mines Saint-Etienne dédié à la recherche en génie des procédés et rassemble environ 80 personnes comprenant enseignants-chercheurs, postdocs, doctorants, stagiaires, et profite du soutien de personnels administratifs et techniques. L’activité du centre SPIN s’inscrit dans le périmètre du Laboratoire Georges Friedel (UMR 5307) et du Laboratoire Environnement Ville et Société (UMR 5600).

 

Ce recrutement est au cœur de la stratégie d’innovation de Mines Saint-Etienne pour permettre à un brevet IMT de se concrétiser en une technologie permettant de capter le CO2 des fumées industrielles, et de contribuer ainsi à l’atteinte de l’objectif Français de Neutralité carbone

data.description:
Pelagon - Autonomous Maritime ISR

Full-time · On-site (Marseille or Paris) · Founding team · Reports to founders

The sea is the physical layer of the economy—the conduit for our energy, communications, and trade. It is also Europe’s exposed flank. Pelagon is building the answer.

Founded by Aymeric (serial deeptech entrepreneur; founded & exited Scortex, Leading AI solution for manufacturing quality) and Gauthier (Navy officer and McKinsey), Pelagon is building a foundational multimodal acoustic model for autonomous maritime protection (underwater and surface) in service of European sovereignty. It will be deployed on a distributed, autonomous network of vectors (UUVs, buoys, sailbuoys, seabed…) to provide real-time understanding of underwater threats.

France and Europe have world-class acoustic engineers and a long history in underwater warfare. By bridging this expertise with modern physical-AI strategies (as seen in autonomous driving and robotics). Europe is still missing it’s naval NeoPrime, Pelagon aims to become to lead the way in autonomous marine protection—from detection to interception—partnering with leading navies, primes, and neo-primes, while also operating its own fleet as a service.

Pelagon is backed by Hexa, the pioneer startup studio in Europe, which has launched 35+ companies, including unicorns like Front, Aircall, and Spendesk, combining €230m+ ARR and €750m raised.


The role

As Embedded System Lead Engineer, you take end-to-end technical ownership of the hardware, electronics, and embedded stack across a small family of autonomous maritime platforms, some operating on the surface, some beneath it.

What they share matters more than what sets them apart: each must persist at sea for long stretches, sense its surroundings, run our AI on-device, and report back intelligently — all while surviving a brutal environment on a very tight energy budget.

You will lead their technical development, from architecture and component selection through bring-up, integration, sea trials, and iteration. You'll set the engineering bar for the platforms team and shape how we build for years to come.

These platforms exist to carry one thing into the water: our AI. Pelagon trains high-performance detection models in-house on its own stack, and those models have to run on-device, at the edge, on a razor-thin power budget — then push results back to our operations center. Designing the compute-and-power architecture that makes this possible is the heart of the role.

The mandate is simple and uncompromising: get reliable hardware in the water fast, and start collecting data. Every week of persistent at-sea operation compounds. The hardware is the gate to all of it.

What you'll own

  • Common system architecture across the platforms: power, sensing, compute, and communications.

  • The edge-AI compute platform — selecting and integrating the processors and accelerators that run our in-house detection models on-device, and extracting maximum inference from every milliwatt.

  • Electronics design and integration — power distribution, battery systems, motor/thruster control, sensor interfaces (acoustic, pressure, IMU, GNSS, AIS).

  • The embedded software and autopilot stack, firmware, and the low-level glue that makes autonomy reliable in a brutal, wet, salty environment.

  • Robustness and efficiency engineering: watertight integrity, power budgets and endurance, thermal behaviour, EMC, and graceful failure modes far from shore.

  • Hands-on bring-up and sea trials — you'll be on the dock and on the boat, not just at the bench.

  • Vendor and component decisions, and the build-up of our test and manufacturing practices as we scale from prototype to fielded units.

The hard problems you'll be solving

These are genuinely difficult, and that's the point:

  • Persistence with a finite power budget. Endurance is everything for a surveillance node — squeezing weeks of useful operation out of a sealed, ship-deployable platform is a relentless optimization problem across power, compute, and duty-cycling.

  • Reliability with no one to fix it. A system at sea has to fail safe and recover on its own. There is no field technician at 30 nm offshore in a 2 m swell.

  • Running real AI at the edge, on almost no power. This is the defining challenge of the role. Our in-house models have to run inference on-device, in real time, on platforms with a razor-thin energy budget — then sense, sleep, and wake intelligently to stretch endurance from hours into weeks. Getting high-performance ML to live within milliwatts is what makes the entire system possible.

  • Sensing in a hostile medium. The ocean fights you at every turn — pressure, corrosion, biofouling, acoustic noise, intermittent comms — and the hardware has to keep sensing and computing through all of it.

  • Speed without fragility. We are building fast toward sea trials, but a demonstrator that breaks doesn't generate data. You'll have to find the line between moving quickly and building things that survive the ocean.

Who we're looking for

You are a sharp, senior builder who wants to own a problem, not be handed a ticket. Specifically:

  • 5+ years building real, shipping hardware — embedded systems that had to be efficient, robust, and survive the real world.

  • Direct experience building drones or autonomous systems. This could come from drone companies (e.g. Parrot), automotive / autonomous vehicles, or the marine autonomy space.

  • Deep, hands-on command of the full embedded stack: electronics design, power systems, motor/actuator control, sensor integration, microcontrollers and embedded Linux, and firmware close to the metal.

  • Comfort with autopilot / flight-controller ecosystems (Pixhawk, ArduPilot / ArduSub / PX4 or equivalent) and the realities of real-time control.

  • Experience deploying AI/ML models at the edge — embedded inference, accelerators (GPU / NPU / TPU-class), model quantization and optimization, and the power-versus-performance tradeoffs that come with it. This is central to what we do.

  • A bias toward action: you prototype, test, break, and iterate — and you're energized by tight deadlines and a mission that genuinely matters.

  • Fluency working in a fast, ambiguous, founding-team environment where you define the process as much as follow it.

Bonus points for: mechanical / mechatronic breadth (you can reason about hulls, sealing, and thrust as well as circuits); experience with subsea or marine hardware; comms in degraded / contested environments; CFD or hydrodynamics intuition; or having taken a hardware product from zero to fielded at scale.

Why join now

  • Founding ownership. You'll be one of the first engineers and will define the technical foundation of the company. Meaningful equity comes with that.

  • A mission with weight. This is hardware that protects critical infrastructure and Europe's maritime space.

  • Real things, in the real ocean, fast. You'll see your work in the water within weeks, not years.

  • AI-first, at the edge, in the real world. We train our own models and run them where it counts: in the water, on the device. You'll be solving the edge-ML and power problems most companies only talk about.

  • A sovereign, European deeptech at the inflection point of a market with strong NATO and EU policy momentum behind it.

Lemonway is a licensed payment institution at the heart of Europe’s new digital economy.

We secure payments for crowdfunding platforms, the collaborative economy, marketplaces and online retailers, with a strong commitment to fighting fraud and protecting funds.

We are looking for a Senior Software Engineer for the Payments Tribe, a critical part of our platform powering the payment experience across all channels. You will report to the Engineering Manager of the Tribe, and work closely with 8 engineers across 2 squads (Core banking, Payments).

You will architect, design, and drive the enhancement of our platform by specifying, implementing, testing, monitoring and troubleshooting the services provided to our customers, working across payment APIs, processing, reconciliation, and core banking systems.

This role combines technical craftsmanship, teamwork and product mindset for a Tribe that is central to both current and future projects for Lemonway. You will play a pivotal role in designing and delivering our next-generation card payment stack for acquiring and issuing, as well as our cash management platform.

Your responsibilities

Technical craftsmanship

  • Design and deliver scalable, complex features that can evolve with the right trade-off between code quality and time spent

  • Lead code and architecture reviews, actively enforcing and shaping the Tribe’s best practices and architectural decisions

  • Drive continuous improvement: stay updated on the latest ecosystem trends, experiment with new patterns, and actively mentors peers to elevate the Tribe’s engineering standards

Domain ownership

  • Take strong ownership of the products we develop, and contribute to all parts of the development cycle from specifying to solving issues that our clients are facing in production

  • Deep dive into our complex payment ecosystem. Ask tough questions, challenge the status quo, and leverage your architectural expertise together with domain knowledge to build resilient solutions

  • Understand the “why” behind the “what”: bridge the gap between technical implementation and business value, ensuring our payment flows directly drive Lemonway’s operational success and client satisfaction

Team player

  • Collaborate closely with software, QA and infrastructure engineers to solve technical challenges, as well as product managers for feature development

  • Act as a technical communicator: translate complex architectural decisions into clear, actionable insights for both technical and non-technical stakeholders

  • Participate actively in our hybrid setup with people at the office, at home, and nearshore

  • Strike the right balance between independent problem-solving and guiding teammates, whilst being solutions oriented in your approach


Your qualifications

  • You have 5+ years of experience in software engineering, building robust and scalable applications

  • You have deep architectural knowledge and proven hands-on experience with Domain-Driven Design (DDD), Hexagonal architecture, Event-Driven Architecture, and Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS)

  • You have strong expertise in relational databases and a proven track record of designing, building, and operating micro services-based architectures

  • You possess excellent communication skills, enabling you to drive technical consensus and collaborate effectively across teams

  • You are familiar with our technical stack based on modern .NET (C#), MS SQL, RabbitMQ, Docker, and Kubernetes

  • You have practical experience in building CI/CD pipelines and using Terraform for Infrastructure as Code (IaC)

  • You are fluent in French and you are comfortable working in English, which is a strong asset given our international environment

  • (Nice to have) You actively leverage AI tools in your ways of working

If you do not meet all the requirements, but believe you can succeed in this role, we encourage you to apply.

data.description:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The team

Mistral is building a sovereign AI cloud for Europe. Our customers in finance, healthcare, and the public sector run frontier models on European-jurisdiction infrastructure, and the Cloud Platform team builds the systems that make that possible — compute orchestration, Kubernetes, bare metal, storage, networking, and the datacenter fleet that runs it all.

We run it all on our own metal, our own network, our own datacenters — which means when something breaks, the fix is ours to write.

European Compute Units let enterprises commit to multi-year capacity on that infrastructure, and we are scaling toward a gigawatt of compute across Europe by 2030. You will design and ship the layer every sovereign AI deployment depends on and shape the team building it.

The Role

This is a people-leadership role from day one. You will manage the team — hiring, coaching, performance, growth paths, honest feedback — while staying close to the code: roughly half your time in architecture decisions and the hardest technical problems the team faces, the other half leading your squad. If you are looking for a senior IC role, this is not it.

You will lead the team building our serverless containers product: the way developers run AI apps, MCP servers, APIs, and managed workers on our cloud without thinking about servers. Push a container, get an endpoint, scale from zero to thousands of instances and back down — across CPU and GPU.

On a hyperscaler, the serverless layer is a product someone else built. Here you own it end to end: the scheduler that decides where a container lands, the routing path a request takes, the machinery that turns a scaled-to-zero service into a warm instance before a customer notices. All of it runs on metal, network, and datacenters we own.

That tension is the product: scale-to-zero economics with cold starts in milliseconds, autoscaling that absorbs a launch spike without a config change, GPUs scheduled onto containers the way other platforms schedule CPU. The customers betting on this layer are the developers building the next generation of AI software on European infrastructure.

What You Will Do

  • Own the container platform end to end: image delivery, placement, request routing, scale-up, scale-to-zero — across CPU and GPU.

  • Make cold starts a solved problem: snapshotting, prewarming, image-layer caching, whatever it takes for scale-from-zero to feel instant.

  • Treat AI workloads as the normal case: GPU-backed containers, streaming responses, long-lived connections, MCP servers that cost almost nothing while idle.

  • Write Go alongside your team and own the architecture and the hardest implementation decisions.

  • Grow the engineers, not just the software — set the standard for ownership and coach people past their comfort zone.

  • Own people management for the team: hiring, performance, growth paths, and honest feedback.

  • Partner with Product Managers to turn platform decisions into a product developers want to deploy on.

What We're Looking For

  • 2+ years of real people leadership. You have managed engineers — hired, coached, given honest feedback, and grown them. Hands-on contribution matters here, but this role is judged on the team you build and lead, not just the code you write.

  • You have shipped production systems in Go. Not dabbled. Shipped.

  • You have built container or workload platforms — orchestration, scheduling, isolation, request routing — not just deployed onto someone else's serverless platform.

  • Deep Linux: namespaces, cgroups, image layers, page cache — comfortable well below the application layer.

  • Multi-tenancy instincts: density, isolation, and fairness when hundreds of customers share one fleet.

  • Significant experience building complex backend or infrastructure systems.

  • You have partnered with product, design, and business teams to ship software that reached real users.

  • A low-ego, team-first mindset. We care less about your exact domain and more about whether you are the kind of technical force other engineers want to work alongside.

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page.

data.title: Embedded Engineer
data.description:
Accelerating embodied AGI.

The next ten years of AI will not be won in software. They will be won in the physical world: in factories, hospitals, kitchens, fields, and homes. The companies that own that data will own the century.

MicroAGI is building it. We are a data research and deployment lab. Atlas captures the manual work inside Europe’s industrial champions, trains foundation models on it, and deploys the right robot onto the floor, with no teleoperation and no interruption to the line. Shift records how physical work actually happens and turns it into training-ready data.

We were founded by former Formula 1 engineers from Red Bull Racing and Mercedes, together with a researcher from the Alan Turing Institute. Our $55M seed round, the largest in German history, was led by Hummingbird with Northzone, LocalGlobe, Village Global, and redalpine. We are based in Munich, with our research centre in Zürich and teams in London, New York, and Istanbul. We are now building the engineering and research teams that will take Atlas into new industries.

Our models learn from data captured in the physical world, by hardware we design and build ourselves. As Embedded Engineer, you will own the firmware that runs on that hardware, from the first register write to the moment data leaves the device, so that what reaches our ML team is clean, synchronized, and trustworthy.

What You Will Do

  • Write and own the firmware for our data-capture hardware: sensors, motion-capture rigs, custom IoT setups, and prototype robots.

  • Build real-time data acquisition: drivers, DMA, buffering, and streaming from many sensors at once without dropping a sample.

  • Solve multi-sensor synchronization, calibration, and time-stamping so every data point lines up across devices and modalities.

  • Bring up new boards with our Electrical Engineer and turn fresh hardware into working devices fast.

  • Build the path from device to dataset: communication protocols, on-device logging, and handoff into our data pipeline.

  • Work shoulder to shoulder with ML engineers. Your firmware decides what their training data looks like, and a timing bug can quietly ruin months of data.

  • Make firmware reliable in the field: testing, OTA updates, error handling, and diagnostics that tell us what went wrong.

Requirements

  • Up to 5 years writing production firmware for embedded or IoT systems.

  • Strong C/C++, experience with an RTOS (FreeRTOS, Zephyr, or similar), and deep familiarity with microcontrollers (STM32, ESP32, NXP, or similar).

  • Hands-on experience with peripheral interfaces and protocols: SPI, I2C, UART, USB, BLE, CAN, or similar.

  • Experience integrating sensors in firmware: IMUs, cameras, depth sensors, force sensors, or similar.

  • A strong understanding of how firmware decisions affect data quality, especially for EMG/EEG sensing: ADC configuration, sample rate, jitter, filtering, and buffering. You know that a great model on a noisy signal still loses to a decent model on a clean one, and you write code accordingly.

  • Comfortable debugging at the hardware boundary with a logic analyzer, oscilloscope, and debugger.

  • Genuinely curious about ML: you read papers, you have trained at least one model end to end, and you understand that dataset quality beats model architecture choice.

  • High agency: you don't wait to be told what to do. You are comfortable in 0-to-1 ambiguity, where the spec is "figure out what the spec should be".

  • Discreet: you handle confidential hardware roadmaps and customer data with care.

  • Fluent in English. German is a plus.

Nice to Have

  • A background in robotics, motion capture, or wearable devices.

  • Experience with real-time or hard-deadline systems: audio, video sync, or robotic control loops.

  • Experience with embedded Linux, time-sync protocols (PTP or similar), or low-power design.

  • Familiarity with ML training pipelines. Even if you don't run them, you can read a training script.

  • Open-source firmware contributions.

  • Experience taking firmware from prototype to small-batch production: test fixtures, provisioning, and certification support.

Who Will Thrive at MicroAGI

Everyone we hire is assessed on the same four traits:

  • Mission and vision: you care about what we are building and why it matters, and your past choices show it.

  • Intensity: you work at a pace that matches the size of the opportunity, and you sustain it.

  • Entrepreneurial: you start things nobody asked for, and you finish them.

  • Raw IQ: you learn fast, reason from first principles, and get sharper when the problem changes.

This is for you if:

  • You would rather own a problem end to end than wait for a spec.

  • You use AI every day, and you can tell a correct answer from a plausible one.

  • You want to work in person, in the office, with people who are very good at what they do.

This is not for you if:

  • You are looking for a predictable 9-to-5.

  • You would forward output you cannot explain.

  • "That’s not my job" feels like a reasonable answer.

How We Hire

We read every application and reply within five working days.

  1. Talent Screen (30 min): a first conversation, both ways.

  2. Technical or Functional Interview (60 min): how you think when the problem changes.

  3. Your Work (60 min): bring something you are proud of and walk us through it.

  4. Leadership (30 min): a conversation with our CEO.

  5. Coworking Day (engineering and research roles): a day building with the team on a real problem.

Then a decision, usually within a few days.

Pay Transparency

Compensation includes base salary and equity. The salary range for this role is shown on this posting.

What We Offer

  • Agency: real ownership from day one, and decisions that actually matter.

  • Freedom: to choose how you solve the problem, without layers of approval.

  • A seat on a rocketship: one of Europe’s fastest-growing deep-tech companies, at the earliest stage.

  • Free food and drinks in the office.

Equal Opportunity

MicroAGI welcomes applications from everyone. We assess candidates on their work and potential, regardless of ethnic origin, gender, religion or belief, disability, age, or sexual identity.

data.description:
About Us

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

The Role

We are looking for a Senior Design Release Manager to join our Airframe Team in Lausanne. In this role, you will bridge the gap between initial mechanical concept and full-scale manufacturing, taking complete ownership of the manufacturing dossier for our composite structures and airframe modules.

From day one, you will drive Design for Manufacturability and Design for Assembly directly inside the design loop, before parts are frozen. You will set and hold the release standard, define geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, manage engineering change orders, and act as the single authority signing off on product transfer gates to manufacturing.

What You Will Do

  • Manufacturing Dossier Ownership: Own and maintain the complete transfer package for your designated airframe module, including controlled drawing packages, bill of materials structures, material and finish specifications, critical characteristics, and acceptance criteria.

  • Design Loop Integration: Collaborate directly with mechanical design engineers early in the design phase to optimize composite layups, bonded joints, tooling interfaces, and tolerance stack-ups while design changes are still fast and low cost.

  • Transfer Gate & Release Authority: Serve as the final authority on product release packages, evaluating transfer readiness against gate standards before handing hardware over to manufacturing operations.

  • Disposition & Configuration Management: Manage engineering change orders and serve as the single technical contact for drawing dispositions, non-conformance reviews, and design clarification requests from the production line.

  • Supplier & Manufacturing Alignment: Work closely with production operations and external suppliers to evaluate manufacturing constraints for composite structures and precision assemblies.

  • Feedback & Continuous Improvement: Analyze initial production build data and floor feedback to refine manufacturing dossiers and update gate standards for future design iterations.

What We Are Looking For

  • Background: B.Sc. or M.Sc. in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Materials Science, or a related technical discipline.

  • Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerance Analysis: Practical mastery of applying GD&T with intent, performing tolerance stack-up analyses, and defining clear acceptance criteria.

  • Composite Structures & Manufacturing: Strong working knowledge of composite materials, layup sequences, tooling limitations, cure cycles, and bonded structural joints.

  • Drawing & Package Control: Proven experience owning released drawing packages, managing structured bill of materials, and running engineering change order workflows.

  • Early Stage Execution: Demonstrated success integrating manufacturing and assembly principles directly into active design reviews rather than conducting post-design audits.

  • Language Skills: Professional proficiency in both English and French to work fluidly across design engineering and French-speaking production teams.

What We Offer

  • Direct ownership in defining the release and manufacturing transfer standards for high-performance defense airframes.

  • Active collaboration with design engineers early in the development cycle where engineering decisions carry high leverage.

  • High-visibility technical impact across fast-scaling, hardware-centric production programs.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

As a Drone System Validation Technician & Remote Pilot, you will be a vital pillar of our flight operations. You will ensure that our fleet of autonomous drones remains operational, up to date, and ready for deployment at all times. You will manage the validation lab and support engineers during complex field testing campaigns.

Key Responsibilities

Fleet Maintenance

  • Perform preventive and corrective maintenance on the drone fleet.

  • Carry out repairs, upgrades, and component replacements.

  • Execute soldering, wiring, and mechanical assembly operations.

Flight Operations

  • Piloting drones during test campaigns.

  • Serve as the safety operator during test flights.

Logistics

  • Manage inventory for spare parts, batteries, and field equipment.

  • Organize transport and gear preparation for field testing campaigns.

Test Execution

  • Run standardized test protocols and checklists.

  • Report results and anomalies to the engineering teams.

Lab Management

  • Keep the workshop and validation lab clean, organized, and secure.

  • Ensure all necessary tools, consumables, and equipment are available and ready to use.

Candidate Profile

  • Technical degree or significant practical experience in electronics, mechanics, or RC modeling.

  • Strong manual dexterity: proficient in soldering, wiring, and mechanical assembly.

  • Rigorous, organized, and safety-conscious mindset.

  • Experience piloting multirotor or fixed-wing drones (remote pilot certification is a plus).

  • Strong interest in hands-on DIY / technical building projects.

  • English language proficiency: A2 level minimum.

  • Willingness to travel for field testing operations.

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

data.title: Characterization Lead
data.description:
At Kandou, we are redeﬁning the economics of AI infrastructure. Our mission is to democratise AI by signiﬁcantly reducing the Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) of hardware systems — a critical barrier to scalable adoption.

Our proprietary MIMO-over-copper technology powers a high-performance, chiplet-based AI memory fabric that is both scalable and energy-efficient. Unlike traditional interconnects, our solution reduces power consumption signiﬁcantly while preserving high bandwidth and ultra-low latency — unlocking unprecedented efficiency for AI training and inference at scale.

As Characterization Lead, you will own performance characterization of Zinal retimer silicon and the Randa Active Electrical Cable (AEC) channel. This is a Principal / Senior Staff individual contributor role with hands-on technical leadership. Your measurements will establish datasheet limits, channel classes and guard-bands for validation, manufacturing and customer specifications. Based primarily in Lausanne, you will work with silicon, signal integrity and validation teams, including channel characterization partners in Taiwan.

Responsabilities

· Lead silicon and channel characterization from measurement planning and bench setup through analysis, limit derivation and documented hand-off to validation.

· Characterize TX/RX SerDes performance across process, voltage and temperature: swing, jitter, sensitivity, equalization, adaptation, CDR lock, BER bathtubs and shmoos.

· Own channel measurements to at least 50 GHz, including de-embedding, insertion/return loss, mixed-mode S-parameters and common-mode and mode-conversion behavior.

· Establish reference-paddle baselines and channel classes by gauge, reach and frequency; correlate HTDR-derived metrics with calibrated VNA measurements.

· Derive datasheet limits and guard-bands from measured distributions, accounting for uncertainty, sample coverage and aging; maintain traceable datasets and limit revisions.

· Assess carrier-loading and forwarded-clock tradeoffs using measured channel data and simulation, and translate the findings into supported configurations and characterization limits.

· Characterize power, energy per bit and thermal behavior across operating modes and corners; investigate equalizer noise amplification and channel/thermal interactions.

· Coordinate shared laboratory equipment and characterization milestones with validation teams; lead technical reviews and deliver limits in time for downstream qualification and screening.

Essential Experience

· 10 to 14 years of experience in SerDes/silicon characterization and/or high-speed channel and signal integrity characterization following degree completion.

· Direct ownership of a characterization program whose results became datasheet limits or qualification thresholds for a shipping product.

· Strong VNA measurement experience to 50 GHz or beyond, including de-embedding, mixed-mode S-parameters (Sdd/Scc/Scd/Sdc) and insertion/return-loss mask interpretation.

· Hands-on TX/RX SerDes characterization, jitter decomposition, BER bathtubs, PVT shmoos and equalization/adaptation analysis.

· Demonstrated common-mode and mode-conversion measurement depth, with the ability to distinguish channel behavior from fixture and calibration artifacts.

· Statistical characterization and guard-band derivation across corners, with clear treatment of measurement uncertainty, sample size and aging.

· Experience with VNAs, oscilloscopes of at least 50 GHz bandwidth, BERTs, jitter instrumentation, thermal forcing and ATE characterization load boards.

· BS in Electrical Engineering or equivalent, with the technical communication and coordination skills to hand off defensible limits to validation and manufacturing teams.

Essential Experience

· Characterization leadership for shipping 100G/lane or 200G/lane retimers, PHYs, AECs or AOCs.

· Deep mixed-mode characterization where common-mode behavior affects information transport and link margin.

· Experience producing datasheet limits that a separate validation team independently qualified.

· Multi-carrier or proprietary coding schemes, including OFDM-style subcarriers and space-time coding, and their characterization implications.

· Published work or patents in channel modeling, de-embedding or SerDes characterization.

· MS or PhD with a concentration in communications, RF/microwave engineering or signal integrity.

If this is the role you have been looking for and you want to be part of a growing Company, with an exciting future then we would love to hear from you. Together We Kandou It!!

data.title: Business Development Representative (BDR)
data.description:
About Rivia

Rivia is a data engine for clinical trial intelligence. It provides data infrastructure and AI-driven workflows for clinical trial teams, enabling biotechs to run studies more efficiently and to demonstrate which patients derive the greatest benefit from new therapies. Biopharma companies are the source of most therapeutic innovation, yet clinical development is frequently slowed by fragmented data and outdated tooling. Rivia delivers a real-time, integrated view across clinical trial data, improving both trial execution and the evaluation of new treatments.

 

Our goal is for Rivia to become the new standard infrastructure for modern drug development, bringing new therapies to market more successfully at a fraction of the cost.

 

We seek highly driven, motivated and talented professionals to contribute to our growing startup.

 

About Rivia's Sales Team

Our Sales team is at the forefront of Rivia's growth, bringing innovative clinical trial technology to biotech and pharmaceutical companies across Europe and the US.

We operate in a complex, high-value B2B environment, where understanding customers, building trust, and creating meaningful relationships are essential to success.

As we scale, we're building a high-performing commercial organization that combines ambition, strategic thinking, and relentless execution.

The Role

As a Business Development Representative at Rivia, you will be a driving force behind our growth, identifying, engaging, and creating opportunities with biotech and pharmaceutical companies across Europe.

This is not a role where you'll simply follow a predefined playbook. You'll help build and continuously improve our outbound engine, experimenting with new approaches, identifying untapped opportunities, and finding creative ways to connect with the right decision-makers.

You'll own your prospecting activities from initial research and outreach through qualification and handover to our Account Executives. You'll develop a deep understanding of the clinical trials industry, our customers' challenges, and how Rivia can create meaningful value for their organizations.

We're looking for someone who is ambitious, commercially sharp, and relentless in pursuing results. Someone who moves fast, takes ownership, learns quickly, and isn't discouraged by rejection. You'll need to be comfortable navigating complex organizations, engaging senior stakeholders, and finding ways to open doors that others can't.

You'll work closely with our Account Executives and commercial leadership, contributing directly to our pipeline generation strategy and the evolution of our go-to-market approach.

If you're excited by the opportunity to build, experiment, exceed ambitious targets, and have a direct impact on the growth of a Series A startup, we'd love to meet you.

Working Model: This role is based on-site in our Zürich office.

What Excites You

  • Building something from the ground up. You enjoy creating and improving outbound strategies rather than simply executing an established playbook.

  • The challenge of opening doors, engaging hard-to-reach decision-makers, and turning cold prospects into meaningful business opportunities.

  • Working in a fast-paced, high-performance environment where ambitious targets, ownership, and measurable results drive your success.

  • Understanding complex industries, learning about customers' challenges, and connecting innovative technology to real business needs.

  • Experimenting with different prospecting approaches, messaging, and channels to discover what works and continuously improve results.

  • Working closely with Account Executives and commercial leadership, contributing ideas and challenging assumptions to improve our go-to-market strategy.

  • Being part of an ambitious startup where your individual contributions directly influence company growth and commercial success.

  • Taking ownership of your results, pushing through challenges, and continuously raising the bar for yourself and the team.

Responsibilities

Outbound Prospecting & Pipeline Generation

  • Own outbound prospecting activities, identifying and engaging potential customers across biotech and pharmaceutical companies in Europe.

  • Build and execute targeted, multichannel outbound campaigns through email, LinkedIn, cold calling, and other creative approaches.

  • Research target accounts, map key stakeholders, and identify relevant decision-makers and influencers within complex organizations.

  • Generate and qualify high-quality sales opportunities, ensuring a consistent pipeline of relevant prospects for our Account Executives.

  • Develop personalized outreach strategies that connect Rivia's value proposition to prospects' business challenges and priorities.

  • Take accountability for individual activity, meeting, and qualified pipeline generation targets.

Commercial Strategy & Market Intelligence

  • Contribute to building, testing, and optimizing our outbound strategy, identifying new segments, opportunities, and approaches to improve pipeline generation.

  • Collaborate with Account Executives to define target accounts, qualification criteria, and effective handover processes.

  • Develop a strong understanding of the clinical trials landscape, including biotech business models, clinical development challenges, and industry trends.

  • Gather insights from prospect conversations to identify market opportunities, refine messaging, and strengthen our commercial positioning.

  • Partner with Sales, Marketing, and Product teams to improve campaigns, customer understanding, and go-to-market effectiveness.

Execution & Continuous Improvement

  • Own and maintain accurate prospecting data, activities, and pipeline information in our CRM.

  • Track and analyze prospecting performance, including outreach effectiveness, conversion rates, and pipeline contribution.

  • Continuously experiment with new messaging, tools, and outreach strategies to improve results and increase efficiency.

  • Proactively identify bottlenecks, challenge ineffective approaches, and implement improvements.

  • Contribute to building a high-performance sales culture based on ownership, collaboration, continuous learning, and accountability.

What Excites Us

  • At least 2 years of experience in B2B outbound sales, business development, or sales development, ideally in a SaaS or technology-driven environment.

  • Proven track record of consistently achieving or exceeding prospecting, meeting generation, or qualified pipeline targets.

  • Strong outbound prospecting skills, with experience using cold calling, personalized email outreach, LinkedIn, and other channels to generate opportunities.

  • A relentless, results-oriented mindset, with the resilience to navigate rejection, persistence to pursue opportunities, and drive to exceed ambitious goals.

  • Strong commercial judgment and curiosity, with the ability to understand business challenges and translate them into relevant sales conversations.

  • Excellent communication and relationship-building skills, including the confidence to engage senior stakeholders and decision-makers.

  • A proactive, independent, and resourceful approach to problem-solving, with the ability to take initiative and deliver results without constant direction.

  • Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage a high volume of outreach while maintaining quality and personalization.

  • A data-driven mindset, with the ability to analyze performance, identify opportunities for improvement, and adapt strategies quickly.

  • Experience working with CRM systems and modern sales prospecting tools.

  • A genuine interest in innovative technology, biotech, and the opportunity to make an impact on how clinical trials are conducted.

  • Professional fluency in English.

Bonus Points

  • Experience selling into biotech, pharmaceutical, healthcare, or life sciences organizations.

  • An existing understanding of clinical trials, drug development, or the pharmaceutical industry.

  • Experience prospecting into complex enterprise organizations with multiple stakeholders and long sales cycles.

  • Previous experience helping build or scale outbound sales processes in an early-stage startup.

  • Experience working with complex technical SaaS products.

  • Familiarity with sales engagement, automation, and AI-powered prospecting tools.

Hiring Process

Our hiring process typically takes 2–4 weeks and includes four stages:

  • Meet and Greet: A 30-minute conversation with our People team to get to know each other, your experience, and what motivates you.

  • Sales Deep Dive: A conversation with our Sales team to explore your prospecting experience, commercial mindset, and approach to generating opportunities.

  • Practical Assessment: A sales-focused exercise to understand how you research accounts, build outreach strategies, and engage potential customers.

  • Meet the Team: Join us at our Zürich office to meet the team, learn more about Rivia, and explore our mutual fit.

 

Our Values

At Rivia, we are committed to excellence, continuous learning, and the success of both our customers and our team. If you are driven to exceed targets, eager to shape the future of clinical trials, and passionate about making a meaningful difference in the biotech industry, Rivia is the place for you.

  • In it to Win it: Approach every challenge with determination, resilience, and a drive, aiming for the best outcomes and solutions.

  • Embrace change: We see change as an opportunity for growth, innovation, and improvement, continuously evolving to stay one step ahead

  • Why not?: Asking why not, instead of why, allows us to show our curiosity, allowing us to challenge assumptions and explore new possibilities.

  • Find the gap: We are curious and we proactively approach identifying opportunities and solving problems before they arise.

  • Collective accountability: We are one team, on one mission and we are committed to shared responsibilities and mutual support, enabling trust and collaboration.

data.description:
Intro

Willkommen bei Sanoptis – einem führenden Netzwerk moderner Augenkliniken und augenärztlicher Praxen mit über 580 Standorten in ganz Europa. Unsere Vision ist es, Wohlbefinden und Lebensqualität durch erstklassige augenärztliche Behandlung zu verbessern. Unser innovatives, dezentrales Modell ermöglicht es unseren Partnerstandorten, unabhängig zu operieren und sich auf die individuellen Bedürfnisse ihrer Patienten zu konzentrieren. Gleichzeitig sind sie Teil eines größeren Netzwerks mit starken Partnern, das ihnen Synergieeffekte, modernste Technik und viele weitere Vorteile bietet.

Dich begeistert ein Mix aus strategischem Gestaltungsspielraum und operativ-kommerzieller Optimierung und Du willst Deine wirtschaftliche Expertise bei einem dynamisch wachsenden Player der Augenheilkunde unter Beweis stellen? Dann sollten wir uns kennenlernen.

In dieser Rolle wirst Du zur Führung und Optimierung der kaufmännischen Aktivitäten mehrerer Augenzentren in Bern die kaufmännische Geschäftsführung übernehmen. Dein Verantwortungsbereich umfasst die strategische Überwachung, das Leistungsmanagement, die Teamführung und die Zusammenarbeit mit funktionsübergreifenden Teams. Dein Engagement für hervorragende Leistungen wird dazu beitragen, die Geschäftsziele zu erreichen, die Patientenzufriedenheit zu erhöhen und das Wachstum der Präsenz von Sanoptis in der Region zu fördern.


In dieser Rolle wirst Du

  • Unsere Augenzentren kaufmännisch leiten: Du wirst den Betrieb mehrerer Zentren wirtschaftlich leiten und dabei die Einhaltung der Sanoptis-Standards in den Einrichtungen sicherstellen.
  • Betriebsergebnisse und Geschäftsziele verantworten: Die betrieblichen Leistungskennzahlen zu Patientenzufriedenheit, Finanzindikatoren, Einnahmen, Ausgaben und Rentabilität wirst Du überwachen. Ferner wirst Du mit den Finanz- und Buchhaltungsteams bei der Entwicklung und Verwaltung von Budgets, Finanzprognosen und Kostenkontrollmaßnahmen zusammenarbeiten.
  • Leistungsziele definieren: Du wirst Leistungsbewertungen durchführen und Ziele definieren. Es ist Dir ein wesentliches Anliegen, für Deine Mitarbeiter und Teams ein positives Arbeitsumfeld zu gewährleisten, das Leistung durch effektive Kommunikation und Zusammenarbeit fördert.
  • Die regionale Strategie planen: Die Formulierung regionaler, strategischer Pläne im Einklang mit unseren übergeordneten Geschäftszielen erarbeitest Du. Hierfür wirst Du eng mit dem Head of Operations sowie Ärzten und Fachkräften vor Ort arbeiten und netzwerken.
  • Wachstum durch Standortentwicklung vorantreiben: Du siehst Wachstumschancen in Deiner Region und erkennst sie frühzeitig, um sie gewinnbringend zu nutzen. Du wirst durch effektive Marketing- und Werbestrategien zur Steigerung des Patientenaufkommens in enger Zusammenarbeit mit dem Marketingteam beitragen. Dein Ziel ist es, einen Ausbau des Marktanteils zu erreichen.


Du wirst zusammenarbeiten mit

  • Einem starken Operationsteam, bestehend aus vielen Ex-Beratern (Bain, BCG, Roland Berger, Oliver Wyman).
  • Leitenden Angestellten und Führungskräften bei Sanoptis, darunter der Head of Operations und das Führungsteam, das für klinische Innovation und hervorragende Dienstleistungen verantwortlich ist.
  • Renommierten Spezialisten und führenden Experten auf dem Gebiet der Augenheilkunde.
  • Einem engagierten und qualifizierten Team von medizinischen Fachkräften und Assistenzärzten.
  • Interdisziplinären Teams in unserem gesamten Netzwerk, einschließlich Technologieexperten, die an den neuesten Fortschritten in der augenmedizinischen Behandlung und digitalen Gesundheitslösungen arbeiten.


Dein Profil überzeugt durch

  • Einschlägige Berufserfahrung in einem anspruchsvollen Umfeld, z. B. in der Strategieberatung (McKinsey, Bain, BCG o.Ä.) oder in ähnlich schnelllebigen Unternehmen.
  • Die nachgewiesene Fähigkeit, Geschäfts- und Finanzanalysen auf Führungsebene zu erstellen und zu kommunizieren. Du erstellst Analysen akribisch und detailorientiert.
  • Unternehmerisches Denken mit der Fähigkeit, große Verantwortung zu übernehmen und Problemlösungen unabhängig voranzutreiben. Eine eigenständige Arbeitsweise mit wenig Anleitung ist essenziell.
  • Nachgewiesene Erfolge im Umgang mit Interessensgruppen, einschließlich der Fähigkeit, ohne formale Autorität Einfluss zu nehmen und Dir eine wichtige Rolle bei der Entscheidungsfindung zu sichern. Du besitzt die Fähigkeit, auch in schwierigen Situationen Konflikte konstruktiv zu lösen und Durchsetzungsstärke zu behalten.
  • Ausgeprägte Fähigkeiten im Bereich Organisation und Prozessmanagement.
  • Exzellente Deutschkenntnisse (C2-Niveau), Französischkenntnisse von Vorteil sowie Englischkenntnisse.
  • Die Bereitschaft, Ergebnisse zu erzielen und Dich in einem schnelllebigen Umfeld mit hoher Verantwortung zu entfalten.


Sanoptis bietet Dir

  • Wettbewerbsfähige Vergütung: Ein äußerst attraktives Gehaltspaket, ergänzt durch einen jährlichen, leistungsabhängigen Bonus, der an individuelle und unternehmensspezifische Leistungsziele gebunden ist.
  • Eigenständigkeit und kreative Freiheit: Die Möglichkeit, Dich zu beweisen, indem Du selbstständig arbeitest und eigene, innovative Ideen umfassend einbringst als Führungspersönlichkeit.
  • Berufliche Entwicklung: Möglichkeiten für kontinuierliches Wachstum und Karrierechancen bei guter Leistung, unterstützt durch Schulungen, Online-Akademien, Workshops und Branchenkonferenzen.

  • Mitarbeiterrabatte: Vergünstigte Konditionen auf zahlreiche ausgewählte Markenprodukte und Dienstleistungen über unseren Partner Corporate Benefits.
  • Körperliches Wohlbefinden: Eine subventionierte Mitgliedschaft bei Wellpass, die Deine körperliche Gesundheit unterstützt.


Gleiche Chancen

Bei Sanoptis schätzen wir Talent, Leidenschaft und Einstellung über spezifische Erfahrungen. Wir begrüßen Bewerber aus verschiedenen Hintergründen und priorisieren gleiche Chancen für alle.

data.title: Embedded Control Engineer
data.description:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.


BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO

  • Architect a breakthrough energy technology – Play a defining role in designing and integrating the systems that will power the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion plant, influencing decisions that shape the future of clean energy.

  • Solve some of the most complex engineering challenges in fusion – Work across magnet design, HTS technology, manufacturing, structural integration, and controls, turning cutting-edge science into real hardware

  • Move fast and build what matters – Join a highly ambitious, multidisciplinary team that combines cutting-edge simulation with hands-on engineering, turning bold ideas into real hardware on the path to commercial fusion.

YOUR IMPACT

In this role, you will play a key part in developing the embedded control platform and will translate functional and control requirements into embedded hardware and software architectures, select appropriate microcontrollers, DSP, FPGA, or other controller technologies, and develop real-time software close to the hardware implementation. data.description:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO

  • Architect a breakthrough energy technology – Play a defining role in designing and integrating the systems that will power the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion plant, influencing decisions that shape the future of clean energy.

  • Solve some of the most complex engineering challenges in fusion – Work across magnet design, HTS technology, manufacturing, structural integration, and controls, turning cutting-edge science into real hardware

  • Move fast and build what matters – Join a highly ambitious, multidisciplinary team that combines cutting-edge simulation with hands-on engineering, turning bold ideas into real hardware on the path to commercial fusion.

YOUR IMPACT

Join our team to work on cutting-edge power conversion technologies, developing solutions that combine high power density, high voltage and current, fast dynamic response, and demanding efficiency and reliability requirements. In this role, you will translate functional and system requirements into robust power-stage solutions. Your work will contribute to optimizing efficiency, thermal performance, reliability, scalability, and power density. WHAT YOU WILL DO

data.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an Analytical Chemistry Specialist – Freelance AI Trainer Project based in Switzerland.

Are you an analytical chemistry expert interested in contributing to the next generation of artificial intelligence? This freelance opportunity allows you to apply your scientific expertise to train and evaluate advanced AI models designed to support scientific discovery, education, and laboratory research. You will assess AI-generated responses to complex analytical chemistry questions, identify inaccuracies, and strengthen scientific reasoning across a wide range of applications. Your work will help improve the accuracy, reliability, and practical relevance of AI-generated scientific knowledge. Working remotely and independently, you will contribute specialized insights to the development of more capable and trustworthy AI systems. This role is ideal for experienced chemistry professionals who enjoy solving complex problems, communicating scientific concepts, and exploring the intersection of chemistry and emerging technology.


Accountabilities
  • Evaluate AI-generated scientific content: Review responses to theoretical and practical analytical chemistry questions, assessing their factual accuracy, logical consistency, scientific rigor, and relevance to real-world laboratory applications.
  • Apply specialized analytical chemistry knowledge: Develop and evaluate scenarios involving spectroscopy, chromatography, electrochemical analysis, quantitative chemical analysis, environmental testing, pharmaceutical analysis, and analytical method development.
  • Assess advanced analytical techniques: Challenge AI models on mass spectrometry, high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), gas chromatography (GC), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) interpretation, trace analysis, titrimetric methods, and related instrumentation.
  • Identify and document model weaknesses: Record reproducible errors, reasoning gaps, inaccurate interpretations, and other failure patterns to support systematic improvements in model performance.
  • Contribute to AI training and evaluation: Provide detailed scientific feedback, propose corrections, and recommend improvements to prompts, evaluation criteria, and testing methodologies.
  • Support scientific quality assurance: Apply principles of method validation, quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC), and analytical data interpretation to evaluate the reliability of AI-generated outputs.
  • Communicate scientific reasoning clearly: Explain conclusions, demonstrate analytical approaches, and document the steps behind technical judgments to help improve model transparency and reliability.

    • Requirements

  • Education: A PhD in analytical chemistry or a closely related chemical science discipline is preferred. Equivalent advanced expertise supported by relevant professional or research experience may also be valuable.
  • Technical expertise: Strong knowledge of analytical chemistry principles, instrumentation, spectroscopy, chromatography, electrochemical methods, quantitative analysis, and analytical method development.
  • Research or laboratory experience: Experience in laboratory-based research, analytical method validation, pharmaceutical or environmental testing, instrumentation-intensive studies, or related scientific applications is highly desirable.
  • Specialized analytical skills: Familiarity with techniques such as mass spectrometry, HPLC, GC, NMR, trace analysis, titrimetry, and laboratory QA/QC procedures.
  • Scientific evaluation skills: Ability to identify factual inaccuracies, assess scientific arguments, interpret experimental scenarios, and distinguish sound conclusions from flawed reasoning.
  • Written communication: Excellent technical writing skills and the ability to explain complex scientific concepts clearly, precisely, and logically.
  • Analytical thinking: Strong critical-thinking, problem-solving, and attention-to-detail skills, with the ability to break down complex problems and document reproducible findings.
  • AI training readiness: Interest in evaluating AI-generated content, identifying model limitations, and contributing to the development of more reliable scientific AI systems.
  • Working arrangements: Ability to work independently in a remote freelance environment, manage assignments effectively, and provide a secure computer and reliable high-speed internet connection.

    • Benefits

  • Competitive hourly compensation: A pay range of $8–$65 per hour, with the final rate determined by expertise, professional experience, and geographic location. The final offer may vary from the advertised range.
  • Remote flexibility: Work remotely from India, with the flexibility associated with a freelance contract arrangement.
  • Meaningful scientific impact: Help shape AI systems that may support scientific education, research, analytical problem-solving, and laboratory workflows.
  • Intellectually stimulating work: Apply advanced analytical chemistry knowledge to challenging scientific questions and emerging AI evaluation tasks.
  • Specialized professional contribution: Use your research, instrumentation, and laboratory expertise in an innovative technology-focused environment.
  • Independent contractor arrangement: Manage your work in a freelance capacity, subject to project requirements and applicable engagement terms.

data.title: Senior Radiochemist
data.description:
ABOUT US

Transmutex is a Swiss company founded in 2019. Transmutex is currently advancing the HI-BEAM (High Intensity Breakthrough Engineering for Advanced Medicine) project, an ambitious programme to develop an industrial-scale facility for the reliable production of medical-grade Actinium-225 (Ac-225), a critical radionuclide for emerging targeted alpha therapies. 

Our team spans nuclear physics, engineering, software, radiochemistry, pharmaceutical and industrial development. Working with research labs and industrial partners worldwide, we are building the production capacity needed for the next generation of cancer treatments.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As the HI-BEAM project progresses from conceptual design into experimental validation, Transmutex is expanding its radiochemistry capability to translate established laboratory methods—supported by collaboration with leading international research institutes—into automated, reproducible, and commercially viable production processes.

We are seeking a Senior radiochemist to actively contribute to the technical design of Transmutex’ s radiochemistry process, in strong collaboration with renowned research labs. You will report to the Head of Extraction unit and be part of a small international team

You will primarily be based in Vernier, GE, with regular travel to Villigen, AG and to partner research labs in North America.

MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES

Process development:

  • Design and optimize radiochemical separation and purification.
  • Collaborate across teams to develop radiochemical processes and methodology.
  • Perform radiochemical and chemical analyses, including alpha and gamma spectrometry.
  • Track radiochemistry developments and adopt relevant innovations and best practices.

Industrialization and operations:

  • Develop the radiochemical process flowsheet, including unit operations, process parameters, material balances, cycle times and waste streams.
  • cale up and transfer laboratory processes to a robust and GMP-compliant production line.
  • Define process, equipment, utility, instrumentation and facility-interface requirements.
  • Support equipment selection, sizing, qualification, commissioning and process validation.
  • Develop operating procedures, batch records, control strategies and consumables requirements.
  • Prepare laboratory and production operations aligned with capacity and customer needs.
  • Train and mentor colleagues.

Compliance, quality, and safety:

  • Work with QA and Safety to ensure regulatory compliance and meet applicable standards
  • Implement and monitor safety protocols and regulatory requirements.

QUALIFICATIONS AND PROFESSIONAL ACHIEVEMENTS

The candidates we are looking for must have:

  • PhD or Master’s degree in Radiochemistry, Nuclear Chemistry or related field
  • A minimum of 10 years of experience in radiochemistry.
  • Proven experience in radiochemical separation and purification with strong knowledge of actinide chemistry.
  • In-depth understanding of radiochemistry processes, equipment and tools.
  • Mastery of characterization, alpha or gamma spectrometry, ICP-MS, ICP-OES, liquid scintillation counting, or comparable analytical techniques.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of safety, radioprotection and GMP regulations and requirements. 
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with ability to collaborate effectively with multiple internal and external stakeholders across disciplines. 
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities to address complex technical challenges.
  • Proven experience in translating lab-scale processes to GMP production line would be an asset
  • Fluent in English. Excellent knowledge of French or German would be an asset

TERMS AND CONDITIONS

  • Start date:          early 2027, and no later than April 2027
  • Location:            Vernier, GE, with monthly presence at Villigen, AG; Switzerland. This position also involves regular travels to North America.
  • Contract:            Full-time, permanent employment contract
  • Package:             We offer competitive remuneration and social security, accident/disability insurance and pension plans; one day per week work from home, as well as five weeks’ paid vacation.

RECRUITMENT PROCESS:

One to two technical interviews with the hiring manager, HR and other Transmutex team members; interview with Management for shortlisted candidates. At least one interview will be organized on-site in Geneva.

80–100% I Visp at least 3 days per week and Basel I Jan2027 start.. 

As Lead Accountant, you are responsible for financial reporting, closing and controls of our Swiss entity in Visp and support our other Swiss entities. You provide functional support to accountants, develop standards and, together with the business, drive the further development of our internal control system, financial reporting and ERP processes. You will work at our Visp site at least three days per week, close to our operational teams.

Your responsibilities will include,

Closing & financial reporting

  • Hold overall responsibility for the monthly, quarterly and year-end closings of our Visp entity under the Swiss Code of Obligations (CO) and prepare the group consolidation, including our other Swiss entities.
  • Support our project to transition to an international accounting standard and own reporting and reconciliations under IFRS or US GAAP.
  • Actively contribute to the further development of our financial reporting.
  • Manage the relationship with our statutory auditors and coordinate audits for the entire group.

Internal control system
